results: 1. Full neurological examination, including eye movements and nystagmus, dysarthria, cerebellar coordination, truncal ataxia, gait, reflexes, plantar responses, strength, sensation, and vestibular testing
cranial nerve examination: supranuclear vertical gaze palsy with preserved horizontal gaze; severe dysarthria and dysphagia
mental status / cognitive screen: MoCA 24/30; frontal assessment battery 13/18
muscle tone examination: severe axial neck rigidity; mild upper-limb rigidity
limb strength (MRC) examination: normal power
deep tendon reflexes and plantar responses: normal reflexes; flexor plantar responses
sensory examination (pinprick, vibration, proprioception): normal
coordination examination (limb and truncal): normal limb coordination; impaired truncal stability
fundoscopy: normal
gait observation including turning and doorways: not recorded
cerebellar testing (dysmetria, dysdiadochokinesia, tandem gait): normal
speech assessment (hypophonia, strained-strangled voice, scanning dysarthria): slurred, progressively unintelligible

DIAGNOSIS: Probable sporadic progressive supranuclear palsy—Richardson syndrome, caused by a 4-repeat tauopathy.

ALTERNATIVE: Corticobasal degeneration presenting with an atypical corticobasal syndrome.

ALTERNATIVE: Multiple-system atrophy, predominantly parkinsonian type.

ALTERNATIVE: Spinocerebellar ataxia or other inherited 4-repeat tauopathy, pending genetic testing.
